title: A cut click, Undo and a dropped clip on a video answer inside 50 ms
goal: On a video, clicking a cut, pressing Undo or Redo, and letting a second clip go on the timeline each still keep the app busy for 57 to 77 ms, over the 50 ms the Premiere goal sets for every press on the timeline. Bring these three under it. This is the part of the edit-speed work that does not wait on the key lane card, so it can be done now. It also finds out whether the 760 ms hold seen right after the second clip lands in the scripted editing session is the app or the walk, and fixes it if it is the app.

log.note: owns these walks: clip-click-cost-walk, undo-redo-cost-walk, an-editing-session-walk

The 760ms hold is the walk, not the app: labelsWhole (step 25) photographs the window and reads its words on the main thread (~700ms) without leaving that off the meter. Reproduced 3/3 (770-783ms); dropping only step 25 read 72ms, dropping only the snapshot still 792ms. Fixed in the harness: labelsWhole excludes its own time, and dropOnTimeline is timed like a press (markers down, meter zeroed at release) so the drop line names the drop's own cost: 67ms (an-editing-session-walk), 75ms (undo-redo-cost-walk).

Cut click: shipped 1d21775e (PanelSectionDeparture: sections leaving while the pick stays on the same clip linger one pass unseen, pulled down the next). clip-click-cost-walk x3: 27/27 cuts 31.7-49.2ms, none over 100 (baseline 47.3-58.7, median ~56). One more run on a build that also carried a since-reverted menu change read 41.6-52.1 (3 of 9 just over 50). Piece clicks unchanged ~20ms. Measured dead ends (not shipped): no-teardown-ever upper bound saves ~12ms on the cut but costs the piece click; dropping the cut's playhead move saves ~3ms; Equatable header menus changed nothing (rebuilds are environment-driven); App Nap opt-out changed nothing.

Undo/Redo not met (Undo 59-71, Redo 44-57): split to undo-and-redo-on-a-video-answer-inside-50-ms with the evidence.
